323194.title: The injectivity conjecture for finitely separated graph C*-algebras
323194.statement:
Let $(E,C)$ be a finitely separated graph. Let $M(E,C)$ be the abelian monoid with generators $\{a_v\mid v\in E^0\}$ and relations

$$
a_v=\sum_{e\in X}a_{r(e)}
$$

for all $v\in E^0$ and all $X\in C_v$. There is a natural map from $M(E,C)$ to the monoid ${\mathcal V}(C^*(E,C))$ of Murray–von Neumann equivalence classes of projections.

**Injectivity conjecture.** The natural map

$$
M(E,C)\to {\mathcal V}(C^*(E,C))
$$

is injective.

This is one of two weaker conjectures introduced after the full monoid isomorphism conjecture, and is intended to be verifiable in situations of interest. The source does not establish it in general.

323220.title: Alpha-beta triangle decomposition conjecture
323220.statement:
Let $\alpha_{m,z}$ be the entries of the $\alpha$-triangle, and let $\beta_{z,y}$ be entries of a triangular array called the **$\beta$-triangle**. **Alpha-beta decomposition conjecture.** The $\alpha$-matrix admits the decomposition

$$
\alpha_{m,z}=\sum_{y=0}^{\lfloor z/2\rfloor}\binom{m}{z-y}\beta_{z,y},
$$

with $\beta_{0,0}=1$ and $\beta_{2y,y}=0$ for all $y>0$. The decomposition was determined experimentally and verified to the extent possible, but remains conjectural.

323656.title: Elekes's general-position rich-lines conjecture
323656.statement:
Let $A,B\subset \mathbb{R}$ with $|A|=|B|=n$, and say that a line is $cn$-rich on $A\times B$ if it contains at least $cn$ points of this Cartesian product. A collection of lines is in **general position** when no two lines are parallel and no three lines are concurrent. **Elekes's conjecture.** For every $c>0$ there exists $C_S>0$ such that, if $m$ lines in general position are $cn$-rich on $A\times B$, then

$$
m<C_S.
$$

The conjecture extends the line lemma discussed in the source and is attributed there to the second author; the paper refers to Elekes for details. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

323845.title: Apostolov–Calderbank–Gauduchon–Tønnesen-Friedman projective-bundle conjecture
323845.statement:
Let $(X,J)=P(E)$ be a projective bundle over a compact curve $\Sigma$ of genus at least $2$. A subbundle is stable in the usual slope-stability sense. **Apostolov–Calderbank–Gauduchon–Tønnesen-Friedman conjecture.** The projective bundle $(X,J)=P(E)$ admits an extremal metric in some Kähler class if and only if

$$
E=\bigoplus_{i=0}^l E_i,
$$

where $E_i$ is a stable subbundle for $1\leq i\leq l$. This conjecture characterizes the existence of extremal metrics on these projective bundles through a decomposition of the underlying bundle. The paper states that, assuming uniformly bounded Calabi-flow curvature, its method provides a proof; the supplied material does not give further details of that proof.

323879.title: Transpose symmetry conjecture for q,t-Narayana polynomials
323879.statement:
For positive integers $m,n$, let $\mathsf{Para}_{m,n}$ be the set of parallelogram polyominoes with parameters $(m,n)$, and let

$$
F_{m,n}(q,t)=\sum_{\mathcal P\in\mathsf{Para}_{m,n}}q^{\mathsf{area}(\mathcal P)}t^{\mathsf{parabounce}(\mathcal P)}
$$

be their $q,t$-Narayana polynomial.

**Transpose symmetry conjecture.** For all positive integers $m,n$,

$$
F_{m,n}(q,t)=F_{n,m}(q,t).
$$

This conjecture asserts symmetry under exchanging the two polyomino parameters. It had been checked in the paper for all pairs with $\max(m,n)\leq9$, but the supplied text gives no general proof or resolution.

323949.title: Brlek–Reutenauer conjecture on factor and palindromic complexity
323949.statement:
Let ${\mathbf u}$ be an infinite word whose language is closed under reversal. Let $D({\mathbf u})$ denote its defect, and let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf u}(n)$ and $\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf u}(n)$ denote its factor and palindromic complexities, respectively. Define

$$
T_{\mathbf u}(n)=\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf u}(n+1)-\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf u}(n)+2-\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf u}(n+1)-\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf u}(n).
$$

**Brlek–Reutenauer conjecture.** One has

$$
2D({\mathbf u})=\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty}T_{\mathbf u}(n).
$$

The conjecture was known for periodic words and had previously been proved for uniformly recurrent words; the source proves it in its general version, so the conjecture is solved.

324150.title: The weak-closedness characterization of F-purity for binomial edge ideals in characteristic 2
324150.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $S$ be the polynomial ring associated with $G$, and let $J_G$ be its binomial edge ideal. Assume that $p=2$.

**Weak-closedness characterization.** The quotient $S/J_G$ is $F$-pure if and only if $G$ is weakly closed.

The preceding theorem proves the implication from weak closedness to $F$-purity for arbitrary $p$. The converse, and hence the equivalence in characteristic $2$, was verified in the source for graphs with at most six vertices using Macaulay2, but remains conjectural in general.

324252.title: The Harmonic index–radius conjecture
324252.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple undirected connected graph with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$ and edge set $E(G)$. Let $d_i$ be the degree of $v_i$, define the Harmonic index by

$$
H(G)=\sum_{v_i v_j\in E(G)}\frac{2}{d_i+d_j},
$$

and let $r(G)$ be the graph radius.

**Harmonic index–radius conjecture.** For all connected graphs $G$ except even paths,

$$
H(G)\geq r(G).
$$

The conjecture is proposed as an analogue of the strengthened Randić index–radius conjecture. The paper proves related bounds in terms of the cyclomatic number, including the asserted inequality for graphs with cyclomatic number at most four, but leaves the general statement open.

324673.title: Bounded arithmetic progressions in ranges of rational polynomials
324673.statement:
Let $g(x)$ be a polynomial over the rationals, and write $g(\mathbb{Q})$ for its range on rational inputs. An **arithmetic progression** is a finite sequence of the form $a+id$ with fixed rational numbers $a,d$ and consecutive integer indices $i$. **Arithmetic-progression conjecture.** For every rational polynomial $g(x)$, there is a bound $b$ such that $g(\mathbb{Q})$ contains no arithmetic progression of length $b$.

This would rule out arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions in polynomial ranges and, together with the preceding additive-combinatorial proposition, would constrain rational polynomials that fail to expand. The authors state that they were unable to prove it and that it would follow from the Uniformity Conjecture.

346734.title: Lacasse's conjecture on the PAC-Bayesian combinatorial sum
346734.statement:
Let $\xi,\xi_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by

$$
\xi(m):= \sum_{k=0}^m \binom{m}{k} \left( \frac{k}{m} \right)^k \left( 1-\frac{k}{m} \right)^{m-k}
$$

and

$$
\xi_2(m):= \sum_{j=0}^m \sum_{k=0}^{m-j} \binom{m}{j} \binom{m-j}{k} \left( \frac{j}{m} \right)^j \left( \frac{k}{m} \right)^k \left( 1-\frac{j}{m}-\frac{k}{m} \right)^{m-j-k}.
$$

**Lacasse's conjecture.** For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\xi_2(m)=\xi(m)+m.
$$

This conjecture arose from numerical evidence in the study of combinatorial sums appearing in refined PAC-Bayesian bounds for majority-vote classifiers. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

372920.title: Support description conjecture for almost vexillary permutations
372920.statement:
Let $w$ be an **almost vexillary permutation**, let $D(w)$ be its associated diagram, and let $\mathcal{SBD}(D(w),\emptyset,A)$ be the stated set of combinatorial objects for a subset $A\subset D(w)$. For such an object $\mathcal D$, write $\mathrm{wt}(\mathcal D)$ for its weight, and let $\mathrm{supp}(\mathfrak G_w)$ denote the support of the Grothendieck polynomial $\mathfrak G_w$.

**Almost vexillary support conjecture.** For every almost vexillary permutation $w$, there exists a subset $A\subset D(w)$ such that

$$
\mathrm{supp}(\mathfrak G_w)=\{\mathrm{wt}(\mathcal D)\colon \mathcal D\in\mathcal{SBD}(D(w),\emptyset,A)\}.
$$

The supplied context does not identify this assertion as proved or refuted, so it is recorded as open. The notation suggests a combinatorial model for the support, but the excerpt does not provide its definitions.

373454.title: Full holonomy conjecture for higher-dimensional Laplacian dynamics
373454.statement:
Let $P(t)$ be the state of Laplacian dynamics on $n$ vertices, let $D(P(0))$ denote its degree matrix, and let $X(t)$ solve

$$
\dot{X}=-L(P)X.
$$

For a base point determined by the dynamics, write $\operatorname{Hol}_p^0$ for the restricted holonomy group.

**Full holonomy conjecture.** For $d\geq 3$, $n>d$, and initial conditions with $D(P(0))$ not scalar (non-regular graph), the restricted holonomy group of Laplacian dynamics is

$$
\operatorname{Hol}_p^0=\mathrm{SO}(d).
$$

The preceding finite-time rank criterion proves full holonomy when sufficiently many curvature-generated skew directions are linearly independent. Establishing that this rank condition holds generically for all $d\geq 3$ would require a transversality argument controlling symmetry strata, so the fully generic statement remains conjectural.

373969.title: Gerke–Marciniszyn–Steger sparse counting lemma
373969.statement:
Let $H$ be a fixed graph. For each vertex $x\in V(H)$, let $V_x$ be a pairwise disjoint set of $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal G(H,n,m)$ be the family of graphs with vertex set $\bigcup_{x\in V(H)}V_x$ and exactly $m$ edges between $V_x$ and $V_y$ for every $\{x,y\}\in E(H)$. Let $\mathcal G(H,n,m,\varepsilon)$ be the subfamily in which every such bipartite graph is $\varepsilon$-regular. Define

$$
m_2(H)=\max\left\{\frac{|E(H')|-1}{|V(H')|-2}:H'\subseteq H,\ |V(H')|\geq 3\right\}.
$$

Let $\mathcal F(H,n,m,\delta)$ consist of graphs containing fewer than

$$
(1-\delta)n^{|V(H)|}\left(\frac{m}{n^2}\right)^{|E(H)|}
$$

canonical copies of $H$. **Counting Lemma.** For any $\beta>0$ and $\delta>0$, there exist constants $\varepsilon>0$, $C>0$, and $n_0>0$ such that for all $m\geq Cn^{2-1/m_2(H)}$ and $n\geq n_0$,

$$
|\mathcal F(H,n,m,\delta)\cap\mathcal G(H,n,m,\varepsilon)|\leq\beta^m {n^2\choose m}^{|E(H)|}.
$$

The sparse counting lemma would provide quantitative control on the number of copies of a fixed graph in sparse regular configurations, complementing the resolved sparse embedding lemma (the KŁR conjecture). Its general form remains widely open.

374530.title: Cosine covariance stochastic domination conjecture for Gaussian minima
374530.statement:
Let $z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_n)$ and, for an $n\times n$ correlation matrix $\Sigma$, define

$$
M(\Sigma)=\min_{1\leq i\leq n}|(\Sigma^{1/2}z)_i|.
$$

Define the cosine covariance by

$$
\Sigma^{\mathrm{cos}}_{ij}=\cos\left(\frac{\pi(i-j)}{n}\right).
$$

**Cosine covariance conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$, every correlation matrix $\Sigma$, and every $t\geq 0$,

$$
\mathbb{P}[M(\Sigma^{\mathrm{cos}})\geq t]\leq\mathbb{P}[M(\Sigma)\geq t].
$$

Thus $M(\Sigma^{\mathrm{cos}})$ should be stochastically dominated by $M(\Sigma)$; in particular, for every $p>0$,

$$
\mathbb{E}[M(\Sigma^{\mathrm{cos}})^p]\leq\mathbb{E}[M(\Sigma)^p].
$$

The paper presents this as a stronger revision of Litvak's refuted moment conjecture and states that it has not been proved; the proposed stochastic domination remains open.

374917.title: Monochromatic finite-sums and product-of-sums conjecture
374917.statement:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\bigcup_{i=1}^m A_i$ be a finite partition, let $\mathcal{P}_f(\mathbb{N})$ denote the nonempty finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$, and let $\alpha<\beta$ mean $\max\alpha<\min\beta$. **Finite-sums and product-of-sums conjecture.** There exist $j\in[m]$, $b>1$, and a sequence $\langle x_t\rangle_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that

$$
\left\{\sum_{t\in\alpha}x_t,\ \prod_{s=1}^b\sum_{t\in\alpha_s}x_t:\ \alpha\in\mathcal{P}_f(\mathbb{N}),\ \alpha_1<\alpha_2<\dots<\alpha_b\in\mathcal{P}_f(\mathbb{N})\right\}\subseteq A_j.
$$

Thus one cell of every finite partition should contain all finite sums from one sequence together with the products of $b$ sums over successive finite blocks, for some $b>1$. The question is stated as open, and an affirmative answer would follow from the paper's return-time conjecture.

374944.title: Alexandersson–Shapiro square-graph cone conjecture for derivative discriminants
374944.statement:
Let $P(t)=\prod_{i=1}^n(t-x_i)$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$, and for $0\le k\le n-2$ define

$$
\mathcal D_k^{(n)}:=\operatorname{disc}(P^{(k)}).
$$

A symmetrized graph monomial is obtained by symmetrizing a product of root differences over labelled graphs. The square-graph cone is the convex cone generated by such monomials whose edges all have even multiplicity.

**Square-graph cone conjecture.** For every $n\ge2$ and every $0\le k\le n-2$, the polynomial $\mathcal D_k^{(n)}$ belongs to the square-graph cone. Equivalently, $\mathcal D_k^{(n)}$ is a positive linear combination of symmetric sums of products

$$
\prod_{(i,j)\in E(G)}(x_i-x_j)^2.
$$

The conjecture strengthens a question of Sottile and Mukhin about expressing these symmetric, translation-invariant discriminants through nonnegative expressions in pairwise root differences. The terminal cubic family $k=n-3$ is proved in the paper, while the general square-graph positivity problem remains open.

375060.title: Robichaux's ghost Kohnert rule for Grothendieck polynomials
375060.statement:
For a permutation $w\in S_n$, let ${\sf GKKoh}(w)$ be the family of ghost $K$-Kohnert diagrams generated from the diagram of $w$ by ordinary, $K$-, ghost, and ghost $K$-Kohnert moves. For $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^n$, let ${\sf GKKoh}(w,\alpha)$ consist of the diagrams of weight $\alpha$, and let $\mathrm{PD}(w,\alpha)$ be the pipe dreams of $w$ of weight $\alpha$.

**Robichaux's ghost Kohnert conjecture.** For every permutation $w\in S_n$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^n$,

$$
\#{\sf GKKoh}(w,\alpha)=\#\mathrm{PD}(w,\alpha).
$$

This proposed correction to the Ross–Yong rule is the conjectured full enumerative model for Grothendieck polynomials. The supplied text gives no resolution, while the paper's results motivate the weaker support conjecture because the full rule may fail by overcounting and undercounting.

375072.title: The combinatorial criterion for kinematic support
375072.statement:
Let $\Gamma_{L^\ast}$ be a graph in the class of loop BCFW graphs $\mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathtt{BCFW}}_{k,n;L^\ast}$, and let

$$
(\mathcal{G}_0,\mathcal{G}_1,\dots,\mathcal{G}_T=\Gamma_{L^\ast})
$$

be the corresponding branch of the loop BCFW recursion. Say that $\Gamma_{L^\ast}$ has **kinematic support** when it satisfies the realizability condition defined in the paper. **Combinatorial criterion for kinematic support.** The graph $\Gamma_{L^\ast}$ has kinematic support if and only if, for all faces $f^\ast,g^\ast$ and all $t=0,1,\dots,T$ for which they are faces of $\mathcal{G}_t$, the faces are $2_{\mathcal{N}}$-separated in $\mathcal{G}_t$ if and only if they are $2_{\mathcal{N}}$-separated in $\mathcal{G}_T=\Gamma_{L^\ast}$. The criterion is presented after an example showing that full $2$-separation alone is not sufficient for kinematic support. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

375229.title: The EF1 conjecture for matroids with a common valuation
375229.statement: Let $M=(E,\mathcal{I})$ be an independence structure, where $E$ is a finite set and $\mathcal{I}$ is closed under taking subsets. Let $\chi(M)$ be the least number of independent sets in a partition of $E$. A **matroid** is an independence structure satisfying the exchange property: whenever $X,Y\in\mathcal{I}$ and $|X|>|Y|$, some $x\in X\setminus Y$ satisfies $Y\cup\{x\}\in\mathcal{I}$. For an integer $q\geq\chi(M)$, $M$ is EF1-$q$-colorable if every nonnegative additive valuation on $E$ admits an EF1 partition of $E$ into $q$ independent sets; a class has the EF1 property if every member is EF1-$q$-colorable for every such $q$. **The matroid EF1 conjecture.** The class of matroids satisfies the EF1 property. This is known for broad classes including base-orderable and regular matroids, but remains open for general matroids; its validity is known to follow from a conjecture of Gabow.

381117.title: The extremely amenable subgroup conjecture for closed oligomorphic permutation groups
381117.statement: Let $G$ be a **closed oligomorphic permutation group**, meaning a closed permutation group with finitely many orbits on $n$-tuples for every $n\geq 1$. An expansion of an $\omega$-categorical structure is **ordered** when it includes a linear order, and is **Ramsey** when its age has the Ramsey property. **The extremely amenable subgroup conjecture.** Every closed oligomorphic permutation group contains a closed oligomorphic subgroup that is extremely amenable. Equivalently, every $\omega$-categorical structure has an ordered $\omega$-categorical expansion that is Ramsey. This is presented as an important variant of the unresolved conjecture discussed immediately beforehand, reformulated in terms of topological groups; no resolution is supplied in the source.
